### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-defaults/ui.json`, `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `939a626eb73c5c9d7f07cdd6085f99471909f788` — the merge of head `d38f8793dd2db5beae60b700a9732e7d24b4b3db` into base `75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 939a626eb73c5c9d7f07cdd6085f99471909f788 && git checkout 939a626eb73c5c9d7f07cdd6085f99471909f788
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8 d38f8793dd2db5beae60b700a9732e7d24b4b3db && git checkout -B drift-repro 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8 && git merge --no-ff d38f8793dd2db5beae60b700a9732e7d24b4b3db

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 75afeffdf564ae0bd4c0baa18791f765d10a91a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Inputs read: the diff `origin/main...pr-26427` (8 files), card #26370 with its triage, brief, ruling 6431302164, claim 6431654503 and os-dev-report 6433196268, the PR body, the head's check-runs, and the gates `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts`, `packages/spec/scripts/lib/authorable-defaults.ts`. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept set does not move.** `GroupNavItemSchema.expanded` stays `z.boolean()`; only `.default(false)` becomes `.default(true)` (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:813`). An authored `true`, an authored `false` and a non-boolean parse exactly as before; the new tests in `app.test.ts` pin all three plus the nested case. Correct.

2. **The default flip is what ruling 6431302164 letter A ordered**, read off the card: `.default(true)`, not B (drop the default) and not C (keep false). Correct and complete on the spec side: the `describe` text, the generated reference page (five tables) and `authorable-defaults/ui.json` all say `true`.

3. **Every reader of a parsed group's `expanded` was found and none assumed `false`.** `NavigationRenderer.tsx:1538-1557` (`explicitOpen`: a boolean is honoured as written, an absent key opens; a group holding the current route opens whatever it declares); `StudioDesignSurface.tsx:2366-2370` (same rule); `UnifiedSidebar.tsx:381` writes `expanded: true` and its comment already says the renderer opens an undeclared group; objectui's own `ui/packages/types/src/zod/app.zod.ts:326` declares `expanded` optional with no default. No test outside `packages/spec/src/ui/app.test.ts` asserts the old default (searched `packages/` and `ui/packages/` for `expanded` in test files). The registry's `validate()` parse is a diagnostic, not the served value (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:5355`), so a raw-registered app (Setup, Account) is still served without the key and still opens; the two groups meant to start closed carry `expanded: false` (`setup.app.ts:116`, `account.app.ts:186`). The dev's served-shape table (8 showcase groups `false` on main, `true` on the branch; Setup and Account unchanged) is consistent with this code; I did not re-measure it.

4. **One reader was missed, in prose only.** `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts:81-82` still says "`GroupNavItemSchema` declares it `.default(false)`". The pin it guards (`expanded` is required on the output side) still holds under `.default(true)`, so no type or test moves, but the sentence now states the published default wrongly inside the package that owns it. One-line fix owed; see ③.

5. **No key is added or removed**, so `authorable-surface/` is untouched, no tombstone and no `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` row is owed, and no D2 conversion exists (a mechanical pass writing `false` into every silent group would defeat the ruling; writing `true` adds nothing). Matches the two cited neighbours of the same class, `18.list-view-edit-inline-default-on.ts` and `18.view-pagination-page-size-default-50.ts`. Correct.

6. **ADR-0087 D3 entry.** File `18.ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open.ts`, id `ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open`: the filename is `shardNameFor(18, id)` as `build-migration-registry.ts:182` derives it. Major 18 is right: `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `18.0.0`, the spec is at 18.1.0, and the neighbour `list-view-edit-inline-default-on` was added to major 18 on 2026-10-22 and shipped in 18.1.0 (tagged 2026-10-24), so appending a step-18 semantic entry after 18.0.0 is the house pattern. Shape matches the neighbours field for field (`surface` without backticks, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`). The printed fields carry no `#NNNN` tracker id (`packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` pins `/#\d{4,5}\b/`); the citations sit in the file comment only. `registry.ts`, `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide are generated and git-ignored, so nothing more was owed in the diff. No `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment is owed: neither default-flip neighbour added one.

7. **`DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR[18]` entry** (`default-changes.ts:670-683`): key `ui/GroupNavItem:expanded`, `from: 'false'`, `to: 'true'` are the exact fingerprints `authorable-defaults/ui.json` moves between; the baseline (origin/main) and the build are both at major 18, so under `authorisingMajors` the row authorises the move. It is the registration `check:authorable-surface` demands before it accepts a moved default, and it is the right place for it even though the claim's file surface did not name the file. The dev's deviation note is accurate. Correct.

8. **Docs state the new default truly.** `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx:146-148` and the regenerated `content/docs/references/ui/app.mdx` tables say a group opens unless it declares `expanded: false`, and that the current route opens it regardless. Searched `content/docs`, `ui/content/docs`, `skills/` and `docs/` for any prose saying groups default collapsed: none remains. `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:168` lists `expanded` with no default; `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md:27` writes `expanded: true`. The `collapsed by default` hits are form sections, field groups and the Recent rail, not navigation groups. `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json:583` records an earlier QA run; the dev noted it as history and that reading is right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26370-nav-group-expanded-default-open.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. Under ruling A of 2026-10-21 the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone; `semantic` requires at least one moved package at `minor` or above, and a moved `authorable-defaults/` shard refuses `none`. `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` is the one correct grade. No `major`, so the launch-window guard is satisfied; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- Declaration lines agree byte for byte across the three carriers: PR body, changeset and claim 6431654503 each carry `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, with no arm. `semantic` beside `yes` contradicts nothing the level gate cross-checks.
- Observation, not a defect: by `clause2-line.mjs`'s own question (does the diff widen a published accept set or public face) a pure default flip answers `no`, and the class neighbour `list-view-edit-inline-default-on` wrote `Clause-②: no`. Here `yes` is what ruling 6431302164 prescribed verbatim and it is the conservative value (it owes this review), so it stands.
- `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is not moved; none is owed for a semantic entry inside the current major.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F1 (owed before ACCEPT; changeset prose, not a contract change): no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition marker.** The class precedent this PR itself cites, `list-view-edit-inline-default-on`, declared in its changeset `**BREAKING** — a declared default moves, shipped as minor under the launch-window convention` and carried the HTML-comment marker `adr-0087: registered list-view-edit-inline-default-on` (see `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:3085-3093`). This changeset carries neither. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states that during the launch window the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition are the only carriers of breaking-ness, and the gates stay green here only because `semantic` adds no breaking signal by definition in `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`breakingDeclaration`). A deployed app parsed through `defineStack` whose silent groups were relying on starting closed changes behaviour with no diff on the author's side, which is the case the neighbour named BREAKING. Remedy: add the `**BREAKING**` line and the `adr-0087: registered ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open` marker to the changeset; the marker resolves at HEAD and is new in this diff, so the gate accepts it. Changeset prose is the seat's ACCEPT face, so this PASS does not cover it.
- **F2 (one line, same PR): stale comment** at `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts:81-82` still says `.default(false)`. Behaviour and the compile-time pin are unaffected.
- **F3 (seat's `Skills-docs:` check):** the PR body reads `Skills-docs: none — ...` while the diff does update `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` and the reference page. `updated here` needs an eval that exercises the key and none does, so `none — REASON` is defensible; the seat decides the spelling at ACCEPT.
- **F4: CI not final.** At the second read of the head's check-runs: 47 runs, 26 success, 7 skipped, 14 in progress (Test Core 1-8, Build Core, Build and E2E UI, Type Check UI, Type Check workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates). Green so far: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, single-writer and claim guards, Lint scoped tooling self-tests. No red. The landing pre-check requires all green; re-read before enqueue.
- Dev `open_questions`: none. `out_of_scope_findings`: the QA checklist history line (agreed, leave it) and the compiled-artifact note (stated in the changeset, the entry and the default-change reason; agreed).
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d38f8793dd2db5beae60b700a9732e7d24b4b3db`
Local-runs: probe — the changeset gates' own exported readers (check-adr-0087-registration readDisposition, check-changeset-no-major breakingDeclaration and the level gate with the PR payload), run read-only to confirm they read the new changeset's marker and banner; no build, no repo write
Scope: `.changeset/26370-nav-group-expanded-default-open.md`, `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts` (the whole diff `061f21af..d38f8793`: 2 files, +5 / -1).

Addendum to record 6433308567 (head 061f21af): the three edits owed before acceptance (the ADR-0087 marker, the BREAKING paragraph, the stale `.default(false)` comment) are present at this head and correct; the earlier PASS stands for the contract, and this record covers the changeset prose it did not.

Rendered by an isolated CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER subagent of seat session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh (`domain:spec#1`), read-only, adversarial to the dispatch's own conclusions.

Inputs read: the diff between the two heads, the changeset and the D3 entry at `pr-26427b`, the merge base `e677770a` (entry absent there), the precedent at `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:3085-3093`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (marker regex at line 2026, `breakingDeclaration` at 704, the `registered` arm at 5074, `MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS` at 525), `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (launch-window header, lines 60-120), `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts` at both the merge base and the head, `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:5383-5400`, `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts:409`, `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:985-999`, the PR body, claim 6431654503 and the head's check-runs, read twice.

### ① The ADR-0087 marker

1. **Spelling matches the gate.** `readDisposition` (line 2026) matches every HTML comment whose text begins `adr-0087:` (whitespace tolerated around the colon), takes the text up to the comment close, and then needs the word `registered` followed by one or more ids. The changeset carries one HTML comment whose text is `adr-0087: registered ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open`. Run through the gate's own exported function it parses to `{ verdict: "registered", ids: ["ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open"] }`.
2. **The id is the D3 entry's id at the head.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open.ts:21` reads `id: 'ui-nav-group-expanded-default-open'`, and that directory is the first of `MIGRATION_LEDGER_ENTRY_DIRS`. It is the only occurrence of the id under `packages/spec/src/migrations` at the head.
3. **Exactly one marker.** `grep -c adr-0087` on the changeset at the head is 1; the gate refuses two or more and refuses none.
4. **The `registered` arm's two tests pass.** The id resolves at HEAD (item 2) and is new in the diff: no file under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries` names it at the merge base `e677770a`, one does at the head. So the gate's "none of those ids is NEW in this diff" refusal does not fire.
5. **The marker is now demanded, not decorative.** At the old head `breakingDeclaration` on the changeset returned `{ breaking: false, signals: [] }` and `readDisposition` reported no marker; at the new head it returns `{ breaking: true, signals: ["BREAKING"] }` and the marker answers it. The gate's PR step ("Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset") lives in the `Check Changeset` job of `pr-automation.yml`, and that job is green on the head, so CI has already run the real gate over this marker.
6. **Placement matches the precedent.** Marker after the two declaration lines, BREAKING paragraph after the marker, then the body bullets, as at `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md:3085-3093`.

### ② The BREAKING paragraph

- **Truth of the remedy.** "The remedy is one key on that group: `expanded: false`." A written `false` is honoured as an explicit close by the renderer (`NavigationRenderer.tsx` `explicitOpen` block, record 1 item 3), and the same changeset's "To keep a group closed" bullet names the two platform groups that already do it. True.
- **Truth of the parse paths named.** `defineStack`: `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:5383` parses with `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` and continues with `result.data`; `apps` is `z.array(AppSchema)` (line 688), so a silent group leaves the parse carrying `expanded: true`. `defineApp`: `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:2023` is `return AppSchema.parse(config)`. A compiled `objectstack.json`: `packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts:409` validates the lowered stack against `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, and the stack it lowers was already built by `defineStack`. The same changeset's "Compiled artifacts" bullet says an artifact that serialised an earlier parse keeps its written `false` until recompiled; the paragraph's "wherever the app is parsed" is consistent with that, since a stale artifact is not re-parsed. True.
- **"shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention".** `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` lines 64-90: during the launch window a breaking change ships as `minor`, the guard forbids `major`, and the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition are the carriers of breaking-ness. The window is still open: no `.changeset/pre.json`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION` major 18 and `@objectstack/spec@18.1.0` (the gate's own lockstep line). The level gate run locally with the live PR payload passes: `semantic` beside `yes`, `@objectstack/spec` at `minor`, no package graded `patch`. The precedent used the same sentence. True.
- **Declaration lines.** `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` compared as UTF-8 bytes across the PR body (fetched at this review), claim 6431654503 on #26370 and the changeset at the head: identical in all three.
- **Observation, not a defect: the quoted old default is a gloss.** The paragraph writes the documented default as `false`, "a group starts collapsed unless the author opens it". At the merge base the describe read only `'Default expansion state in sidebar'`, and no page under `content/docs/ui`, `content/docs/references/ui`, `skills` or the upgrade guide carried that sentence. The quoted words describe what `false` meant; they are not a quotation. The precedent used the same construction, so this is house style, and the claim it makes (default `false`, a silent group started closed when parsed) is true.
- The paragraph's victim case (an advanced, developer or diagnostics section the author left silent) is the right one: it is exactly the class the two platform apps guard with a written `false`.

### ③ The comment fix

- `packages/spec/src/ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts:82`: `.default(false)` becomes `.default(true)` in the doc comment. One line, and the sentence around it stays true: the default is still declared, so a parsed group still carries `expanded`, which is the pin the suppression guards.
- Nothing else moved: `git diff --stat` between the heads is 2 files, 5 insertions, 1 deletion; the changeset gains the marker, the BREAKING paragraph and two blank lines, and the assertions file changes the one word.
- **CI on the head, as it stands** (read at 2026-10-27T04:02Z): 43 check-runs, 24 success, 5 skipped (opt-in harnesses, Dogfood shard template, Temporal conformance), 14 in progress: Test Core 1-8, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build Core, Type Check debt ledger, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates. No failure. Green and relevant here: `Check Changeset` (holds the ADR-0087 disposition step and the level gate), `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` job, `Type Check · source gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, the single-writer and claim guards. In progress is not a pass; re-read before enqueue.
- F3 of record 1 (`Skills-docs:` spelling) is unchanged and remains the seat's call at ACCEPT. PR author is still `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
